observation.visible_scene: A dark night sky in which several firework bursts are visible at once, each appearing as a cluster of thin radial streaks (white-to-pink) tipped with bright points, accompanied by greyish smoke clouds. The bursts occupy two main regions, left-of-center and right-of-center, and overlap in time.
visible_changes: Frames 1-15: a dense left burst and a sparser right burst are both already mid-explosion; their streaks progressively shorten and dim while the bright end-points linger as scattered sparks, so the left burst fades to a faint core by frame 15.
Frame 16: a new compact orange starburst ignites on the right side while the left region holds only residual dots, indicating a fresh detonation rather than continued motion of the prior burst.
Frames 17-23: that right-side burst expands into a fuller radial cluster of streaks, then begins to fade; the left side remains mostly scattered faint sparks.
Frame 24: a bright flash with a large smoke plume appears left-of-center (a new burst detonating), while the right burst from 17-23 is still visible as streaks.
Frames 25-33: the new left burst expands into a dense radial pattern and the right burst continues to fade, so the two regions again hold overlapping but differently-aged bursts.

Frames 34-41: the left burst's streaks thin and dim into drifting points; a short vertical orange trail (a rising spark/rocket) briefly appears near the bottom edge around frames 34-36; by frame 41 only scattered sparks and a small mid-right cluster remain.
Throughout, the bright points drift slowly downward/outward relative to their burst centers, consistent with falling sparks rather than camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What launched or ignited each burst (no shells, launchers, or ground are visible).
The moments just before t=0 and after t=2.67s, so whether each burst fully completes or new ones follow is unknown.
Whether the bottom vertical trail develops into an explosion after the clip ends.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: the black background gives no reference, but burst positions stay roughly fixed in frame, suggesting a largely static view.
The faint bottom trail (frames 34-36) could be a rising rocket, a falling spark, or a reflection; its identity is not established.
Exact timing of new detonations vs. re-ignition of lingering embers is hard to separate where bursts overlap.
